title: U.S. House · Connecticut's 5th District
area: Northwestern and north-central Connecticut, including Waterbury, Danbury, New Britain, and Torrington

context.text: The Democratic primary was canceled and incumbent Jahana Hayes advanced without appearing on the ballot. Chris Shea defeated Jonathan De Barros in the Republican primary, winning 81% of the vote. The Cook Political Report rated this district D+3 based on 2024 presidential results, making it the most competitive of Connecticut's five U.S. House seats.

summary.text: Jahana Hayes is the Democratic incumbent for Connecticut's 5th Congressional District, first elected in 2018. A former public-school teacher and 2016 National Teacher of the Year, she serves on the House Agriculture and Education and Workforce committees.

background.text: Born in Waterbury, Connecticut, in 1973; earned an associate degree from Naugatuck Valley Community College, a bachelor's degree from Southern Connecticut State University, and graduate degrees from the University of Saint Joseph and the University of Bridgeport.
Worked as a public-school teacher before running for Congress.
Has represented Connecticut's 5th District in the U.S. House since 2019, currently serving her fourth term.

record.text: Serves on the House Committee on Agriculture and the Committee on Education and the Workforce in the 2025–2026 Congress.
Chaired the Agriculture Subcommittee on Nutrition, Oversight, and Department Operations in the 2021–2022 Congress.
Served as ranking member of the Agriculture Subcommittee on Nutrition, Foreign Agriculture, and Horticulture in the 2023–2024 Congress.
